theme: Sperm-egg fertilization: capacitation, motility, zona penetration, egg activation
story: At the centre is fertilization as a step-by-step sequence: the sperm interacts with cumulus cells and the zona pellucida, undergoes the acrosome reaction, penetrates the zona and binds the oocyte membrane. Regulation of capacitation and of flagellar/ciliary motility supplies the competent, motile sperm, while egg activation and negative regulation of fertilization (the block to polyspermy) cover the oocyte side. Together the cluster describes how a single sperm reaches, fuses with and activates the egg.

theme: Phosphate homeostasis via FGF23-Klotho, PTH and renal NaPi transporters
story: The centre is control of sodium-dependent phosphate transport in the kidney, carried by the NaPi-II transporters SLC34A1 and SLC34A3, whose inherited defects cause hypophosphatemic rickets and nephrolithiasis/osteoporosis. FGFR1c-Klotho activation (the FGF23 receptor) and the PTH response are the two hormonal inputs that tune phosphate reabsorption, and bone mineralization is the downstream tissue output. The cluster is the endocrine-renal-skeletal axis that keeps blood phosphate right for building bone.

theme: Urea cycle, ammonia detoxification and its inherited enzyme defects
story: The urea cycle sits at the centre, with its intermediates (citrulline, ornithine, arginine, aspartate) as the connected metabolic processes. The disease pathways cover a defect at each step: CPS1, the ornithine carrier SLC25A15, ASS1, ASL and ARG1. Transcriptional repression of the cycle's enzymes and the cellular response to ammonium act as regulation and trigger, so the cluster as a whole describes how the liver turns toxic ammonia into urea and what happens when a step fails.

theme: Embryonic heart development: chambers, septa, valves, conduction system
story: The centre is cardiac morphogenesis: from mesoderm specification and the secondary heart field, through heart tube formation and left/right looping, to building the chambers (trabecular and compact ventricular myocardium, atrial tissue). Septation and valve formation (outflow tract, atrial and membranous septa, AV canal, pulmonary valve), the conduction system (AV node, His-Purkinje), coronary vessels and pericardium make up the specialised parts. Cardiomyocyte fate, proliferation, apoptosis and sarcomere organization, along with TFAP2 transcription factors, are the cellular and regulatory machinery behind them, so the cluster describes how the whole heart is built.

theme: Mineralization of teeth and bone: dentin, enamel and phosphate signals
story: The centre is hard-tissue mineralization: dentinogenesis, enamel mineralization (with SLC24A4 amelogenesis imperfecta), bone mineralization and tooth eruption. Responses to PTH and phosphate, FGFR-MAPK signalling and chondrocyte development supply the hormonal, mineral and developmental inputs. Post-translational protein phosphorylation probably stands for the phosphorylation of secreted matrix proteins that control crystal growth. As a whole, the cluster covers how teeth and bone build and mineralize their matrix.

theme: Transition metal transport and homeostasis: zinc, iron, copper, manganese
story: The centre is moving essential metals across membranes: zinc import and efflux by the SLC39/ZIP and SLC30/ZnT families, iron import, transferrin and heme transport, and copper and manganese transport. MTF1-driven gene expression and the responses to zinc, iron, cadmium, lead, cobalt and selenium are the sensing and stress side, including handling of toxic metals that use the same carriers. Disease pathways (SLC11A2 anemia, ferroportin hemochromatosis, aceruloplasminemia, zinc-deficiency acrodermatitis) show what transporter failure looks like, so the cluster describes how cells and the body take up, distribute and balance trace metals.

theme: Early neural axis patterning: forebrain, midbrain-hindbrain, rhombomeres
story: The centre is regional patterning of the early neural plate and tube along both axes: forebrain and anterior head development, the midbrain-hindbrain boundary, rhombomere segmentation with anterior HOX activation, and the posterior neural plate. Dorsal/ventral axis specification, boundary formation and neural crest fate commitment set up compartments and their edges, and adenohypophysis development is an anterior head derivative. Generic signal-to-gene-expression transduction is the signalling that ties it together, so the cluster describes how the embryonic brain is divided into distinct regions.

theme: Actin remodelling for membrane ruffles, macropinocytosis and podosomes
story: The centre is control of actin filament dynamics: Arp2/3 nucleation, barbed-end capping, depolymerization and crosslinking. These drive the actin-rich membrane structures (ruffles, podosomes) and the uptake processes that depend on them, macropinocytosis and pinocytosis. Caspase cleavage of cytoskeletal proteins is the apoptotic dismantling of the same scaffold, so the cluster describes how the cortical actin network is built, reshaped and torn down at the cell surface.

theme: Chondrogenesis and skeletal development from mesenchymal condensation to ossification
story: The centre is the cartilage lineage: mesenchymal condensation, chondroblast differentiation, chondrocyte proliferation (positive and negative control) and growth-plate chondrocyte development, with RUNX2 driving maturation toward hypertrophy. Mesenchymal stem cell differentiation feeds the lineage, while tendon development and direct (intramembranous) ossification are neighbouring connective-tissue and bone fates from the same progenitors. Together the cluster describes how the skeleton forms from mesenchyme.

theme: Catecholamine reuptake by dopamine and norepinephrine transporters
story: The centre is reuptake of norepinephrine and other catecholamines from the synapse, which ends their signalling. The dopamine transporter SLC6A3 and the norepinephrine transporter SLC6A2 are the carriers, and their defects cause infantile parkinsonism-dystonia and orthostatic intolerance. The cluster is about catecholamine clearance and what happens when it fails.

theme: Ureteric bud formation and branching in kidney development
story: The centre is the ureteric bud: how it forms, elongates and branches as the metanephric kidney develops. Epithelial tube formation is the underlying cell process, and the positive and negative regulation of metanephros and kidney development, including kidney size, set how far branching goes. The cluster describes how branching of the ureteric bud builds the collecting system and determines how big the kidney gets.

theme: Deoxyribonucleotide metabolism: purine and pyrimidine synthesis and catabolism
story: The centre is the turnover of deoxyribonucleosides and deoxynucleotides: the dAMP, dGMP, dCMP and dUMP processes, deoxyribonucleoside catabolism and purine deoxynucleotide biosynthesis. Pyrimidine catabolism is the breakdown route, and ADA deficiency, where toxic deoxyadenosine builds up, is the clinical example. The cluster is about keeping the dNTP pool for DNA synthesis balanced by making, recycling and degrading deoxynucleotides.

theme: Death receptor signalling: caspase-8 apoptosis, c-FLIP control, necroptosis
story: The centre is extrinsic apoptosis via death domain receptors: FasL and TRAIL signalling recruit procaspase-8, which dimerizes and activates. c-FLIP and other caspase-8 inhibition, together with negative regulation of TNF and death receptor signalling, are the brakes. When caspase-8 is blocked the same receptors switch to necroptosis, and defence against tumour cells is the immune function this serves, so the cluster describes how death receptors choose between apoptotic and necroptotic cell killing.

theme: GABA neurotransmitter lifecycle: synthesis, vesicle loading, release, uptake, degradation
story: The centre is the GABA cycle: GABA biosynthesis from glutamate, loading into synaptic vesicles, secretion, import back into cells, and degradation by the GABA shunt. Alkanesulfonate transport most likely reflects GABA-family transporters that also carry taurine-like sulfonates. The cluster as a whole describes how inhibitory GABA signalling is supplied and ended.

theme: Complement cascade activation and its regulation
story: The centre is complement activation via the classical (antibody), alternative and newer GZMK routes, all meeting at C3 and C5 activation. Regulation of the cascade and of the classical pathway, plus opsonization, are the control and effector sides, and the hallmark complement set summarises the program. The cluster describes how this innate immune system is triggered, amplified, aimed at targets and kept in check.

theme: VEGF-driven sprouting angiogenesis
story: The centre is sprouting angiogenesis: endothelial activation, proliferation, tube morphogenesis and vessel branching. Making more VEGF and boosting VEGF receptor signalling drive the process, and the hallmark angiogenesis set summarises it. The cluster describes how new blood vessels sprout from existing ones under VEGF control.

theme: Base excision DNA repair and its glycosylase defects
story: The centre is base excision repair: DNA glycosylases cut out damaged purines and pyrimidines, APEX1 takes over the AP site, and repair finishes by POLB single-nucleotide or PCNA-dependent long-patch synthesis, overlapping with single-strand break repair. The disease pathways cover defective OGG1, MUTYH, NTHL1 and NEIL3, and NEIL3 also resolves interstrand crosslinks. The cluster describes how small oxidative and other base lesions are fixed and what goes wrong when the glycosylases fail.

theme: p53 regulation in DNA damage, senescence and cell-cycle control
story: The centre is TP53: control of its degradation (MDM2/COP1, and the ARF pathway whose p14ARF defects let cells escape oncogene and oxidative-stress senescence) and cancer loss-of-function through failed tetramerization. Downstream are p53's outputs: DNA repair gene transcription and intrinsic apoptosis after DNA damage, while GTSE1 and MASTL tie in the G2/M checkpoint and recovery into mitosis. The cluster describes the p53 tumour-suppressor axis that decides between arrest, repair, senescence and death.

theme: Neuroendocrine control of stress, arousal and innate behaviours
story: The centre is behaviour driven by stress and arousal signals: responses to CRH and corticosterone, amygdala development and fear, and orexin/neuropeptide FF/QRFP receptor signalling that controls wakefulness. Innate motivated behaviours (exploration, grooming, drinking, mating, parental care) and the response to ethanol are the behavioural outputs, with enhanced nerve impulse transmission as the neural basis. The cluster as a whole describes how neuropeptide and stress-hormone systems shape arousal, emotion and survival behaviours.

theme: Ribosomal RNA transcription by RNA polymerases I and III
story: The centre is RNA polymerase I transcription of rDNA, step by step: preinitiation complex assembly, promoter opening, elongation and termination. Nucleolar chromatin organization by the activating B-WICH and repressive NoRC complexes, plus general negative regulation, set rRNA output. 5S rRNA transcription by RNA polymerase III completes the set of rRNAs, so the cluster describes how cells make ribosomal RNA for ribosome biogenesis.

theme: Renin-angiotensin control of blood pressure and fluid balance
story: The centre is the renin-angiotensin system: angiotensinogen is processed into angiotensins, angiotensin levels are regulated, and the angiotensin receptor signals. Its effects include vasoconstriction and arterial smooth muscle contraction, renal sodium and urine handling, blood volume and thirst/drinking, with opposing vasodilatory cGMP and blood pressure-lowering processes as the counterweight. Neuropeptide catabolism (peptidase processing) and epinephrine transport fill in the hormonal context, so the cluster describes the hormonal regulation of systemic and pulmonary blood pressure and body fluid.

theme: Anion transport and pH balance, with mineralization disorders
story: The centre is transmembrane movement of inorganic anions, meaning bicarbonate, chloride, sulfate and phosphate, through SLC26 and SLC4 exchangers, alongside carbonic anhydrase CO2 hydration and proton transport for pH control. Disease pathways show what this supports in different tissues: chloride diarrhoea (SLC26A3), Pendred syndrome (SLC26A4), proximal renal tubular acidosis (SLC4A4). A second strand is mineralization (enamel via SLC24A4, ectopic calcification in PXE/ABCC6 and basal ganglia via SLC20A2), so the cluster describes how anion and pH handling across epithelia shapes ion balance and where minerals get deposited.

theme: Heme biosynthesis, transport and iron supply for hemoglobin
story: The centre is heme biosynthesis through porphyrin intermediates, which feeds hemoglobin production, with the hallmark heme metabolism set summarising the erythroid program. Iron import, organism-level iron homeostasis and iron-sulfur cluster assembly provide the iron, while heme transport, assimilation and plasma heme scavenging handle heme outside its site of synthesis. Oxygen detection and superoxide and selenium responses point to oxygen and redox handling, so the cluster describes how cells make, move and recycle heme for oxygen transport.

theme: MHC class I antigen processing and cross-presentation to CD8 T cells
story: The centre is MHC class I presentation: endogenous peptides are processed, peptides are loaded onto class I molecules in the ER, and exogenous antigens are cross-presented from endosomes and phagosomes. Cytosol-to-ER transport and ER-associated degradation (Vpu-mediated CD4 degradation uses the same retrotranslocation/proteasome route) supply peptides, and the endosomal/vacuolar pathway is the alternative cross-presentation route. CD8 T cell homeostasis is the downstream consumer, so the cluster describes how cells display peptides to cytotoxic T cells.

theme: Nucleotide sugar synthesis and Golgi transport for glycosylation
story: The centre is making activated sugar donors: UDP-GlcNAc via the hexosamine route from fructose-6-phosphate, UDP-glucose and UDP-glucuronate, and CMP-sialic acid from sialic acid metabolism. The SLC35 family (and SLC33A1 acetyl-CoA) move these donors into the Golgi/ER, and their defects cause congenital disorders of glycosylation and related neurological syndromes. The cluster describes the supply chain of sugar donors that glycosylation depends on.

theme: Epithelial-mesenchymal branching morphogenesis of lung and glands
story: The centre is lung development: branching and bud elongation, lobe and saccule formation, bronchial and tracheal tissues, and type I/II pneumocyte differentiation. These are driven by epithelial-mesenchymal signalling and controlled mesenchymal and epithelial proliferation. Salivary, lacrimal and mammary glands, the bile duct and limb bud use the same bud-and-branch program, with ductus arteriosus closure as a perinatal neighbour, so the cluster describes how branched epithelial organs are built through epithelium-mesenchyme crosstalk.

theme: Collagen and basement membrane matrix anchoring cells via integrins
story: The centre is assembly of the extracellular matrix: collagen biosynthesis, fibril organization and crosslinking, anchoring fibrils, basement membrane assembly and ECM proteoglycans. Integrin interactions, hemidesmosomes and collagen-receptor (DDR) signalling are how cells attach to and read this matrix. The cluster describes the structural matrix and the adhesion complexes that anchor epithelia and tissues to it.

theme: Repulsive axon guidance in neuronal circuit wiring
story: The centre is axon guidance, especially chemorepulsion and inhibition of axon extension, which steer growth cones along the anterior/posterior axis. Serotonergic and dopaminergic axon guidance are specific monoaminergic tracts that use these cues, and dorsal root ganglion development is a sensory neuron population whose projections are guided the same way. The cluster describes how repulsive cues route growing axons to their targets.

theme: Nucleotide sugar transport and N-glycosylation; congenital glycosylation disorders
story: The centre is SLC35 transport of nucleotide sugars into the Golgi/ER (CMP-sialic acid, UDP-galactose, UDP-GlcNAc, GDP-fucose), whose defects cause congenital disorders of glycosylation. UDP-glucose and UDP-glucuronate formation and dolichyl-phosphate-glucose synthesis supply the donors, and N-linked glycosylation is where they are used. Lysosomal oligosaccharide catabolism is the breakdown end, so the cluster describes how glycans are supplied, built onto proteins and degraded.

theme: ER membrane contact sites and non-vesicular lipid transfer
story: The centre is lipid transfer between the ER and other membranes at contact sites: ER-plasma membrane tethering, phospholipid transfer, and PI/PC exchange between ER and Golgi, with PI synthesis in the ER as the source. ER tubular network shaping, membrane bending and ER positioning provide the membrane structure these contacts need, and vesicle-mediated cholesterol transport is the parallel vesicular route. The cluster describes how the ER's shape and its contacts with other organelles distribute lipids around the cell.
